stories.headline: Adaption Launches AutoScientist, an AI Tool That Automates the Model-Training Research Loop

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Adaption introduced AutoScientist, a system that automates the full research loop behind model training and alignment by co-optimizing training data and model recipes until quality converges on the user's objective.
key_facts.excerpt: Today we're introducing AutoScientist, a system that self-improves and automates the full research loop behind model training and alignment. AutoScientist co-optimizes your data and model training recipes automatically, self-improving across both until quality converges on your objective.

key_facts.fact: CEO Sara Hooker, formerly VP of AI research at Cohere, said the tool co-optimizes both data and model and 'suggests we can finally allow for successful frontier AI trainings outside of these labs.'
key_facts.excerpt: “What's super exciting about it is that it co-optimizes both the data and the model, and learns the best way to basically learn any capability,” Hooker told TechCrunch. “It suggests we can finally allow for successful frontier AI trainings outside of these labs.”

key_facts.fact: Adaption says AutoScientist more than doubled win-rates across different models, with aggregate win-rate rising from 48% to 64% when AutoScientist was used instead of an AI researcher's recommendation.
key_facts.excerpt: In aggregate, win [rate moved from] 48% to 64% when AutoScientist was used instead of the AI researcher recommendation.

key_facts.fact: AutoScientist builds on Adaption's existing Adaptive Data product and is being offered free for the first 30 days after release; conventional benchmarks like SWE-Bench or ARC-AGI do not apply because the system adapts models to specific tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: Since the system is built to adapt models to specific tasks, conventional benchmarks like SWE-Bench or ARC-AGI aren't applicable... the lab is making the tool free to use for the first 30 days after its release.

stories.headline: Claude Mythos Preview Becomes First AI to Complete Both of UK AISI's Cyber Ranges

key_facts.fact: A newer Claude Mythos Preview checkpoint became the first AI model to complete both of the UK AI Security Institute's cyber ranges, which simulate cyberattacks on small, undefended enterprise networks.
key_facts.excerpt: In AISI's latest testing, the newer Mythos Preview checkpoint completed both our cyber ranges... This was the first time that a model completed the second of our two cyber ranges.

key_facts.fact: The checkpoint solved the 32-step corporate network attack range 'The Last Ones' in 6 of 10 attempts and the previously unsolved operational-technology range 'Cooling Tower' in 3 of 10 attempts.
key_facts.excerpt: The newer Mythos Preview checkpoint completed both our cyber ranges, solving the range 'The Last Ones' in 6 of 10 attempts and the previously unsolved 'Cooling Tower' in 3 of 10 attempts.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's GPT-5.5 solved 'The Last Ones' in 3 of 10 attempts and did not complete 'Cooling Tower'.
key_facts.excerpt: GPT-5.5 solved 'The Last Ones' on 3 of 10 attempts.

key_facts.fact: AISI estimated in February 2026 that the length of cyber tasks frontier models can complete had been doubling every 4.7 months since late 2024, down from an 8-month estimate in November 2025; Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5 substantially exceeded both trends.
key_facts.excerpt: In February 2026, we internally estimated that the length of cyber tasks AI models could complete had doubled every 4.7 months since late 2024 – already an acceleration from our November 2025 estimate of 8 months. Since then, AISI reported on two new models, Claude Mythos Preview and GPT-5.5, which substantially exceeded both doubling rate trends.

key_facts.fact: AISI's cyber range experiments give each model a budget of up to 100 million tokens per attempt, and recent models disproportionately benefit from higher token limits.
key_facts.excerpt: In our cyber range experiment we use up to 100M tokens and find performance would likely still improve beyond that budget, especially for recent models, which disproportionately benefit from higher token limits.

stories.headline: Anthropic Restores Third-Party Agent Access With New Agent SDK Credits Starting June 15

key_facts.fact: On May 13, Anthropic announced a new 'Agent SDK' credit category for paid Claude subscribers, reversing its April 2026 policy that had barred third-party agents like OpenClaw from running on Claude subscriptions.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic announced via its official developer communications account on X, @ClaudeDevs, that it is changing its Claude paid subscription tiers, introducing a new subcategory of 'Agent SDK' credits for all paid subscribers, which they can now allocate specifically for 'programmatic' uses, including external, third-party agents such as OpenClaw.

key_facts.fact: Starting June 15, 2026, Claude Agent SDK and `claude -p` usage will no longer count toward a plan's regular usage limits; eligible Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users instead claim a separate monthly credit.
key_facts.excerpt: Starting June 15, 2026, Claude Agent SDK and `claude -p` usage no longer counts toward your Claude plan's usage limits. Your subscription usage limits stay the same and stay reserved for interactive use of Claude Code, Claude Cowork, and Claude.

key_facts.fact: Monthly Agent SDK credit amounts are $20 for Pro, $100 for Max 5x, $200 for Max 20x, $20 for Team Standard seats, $100 for Team Premium seats, and $20 to $200 for Enterprise plans.
key_facts.excerpt: Pro $20 | Max 5x $100 | Max 20x $200 | Team (Standard seats) $20 | Team (Premium seats) $100 | Enterprise (usage-based) $20 | Enterprise (seat-based Premium seats) $200

key_facts.fact: The credit covers the Agent SDK, the `claude -p` non-interactive command, the Claude Code GitHub Actions integration, and third-party apps that authenticate with a Claude subscription; API key users are unaffected and keep pay-as-you-go billing.
key_facts.excerpt: The Agent SDK monthly credit applies to: The `claude -p` command in Claude Code (non-interactive mode); The Claude Code GitHub Actions integration; Third-party apps that authenticate with your Claude subscription through the Agent SDK.

key_facts.fact: The April 2026 prohibition was introduced after some subscribers paying $20 to $200 per month consumed hundreds or thousands of dollars of tokens through OpenClaw and similar autonomous agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Some Claude subscribers were paying $20 to $200 per month under Anthropic's Claude Pro and Max subscriptions, but consuming hundreds, even thousands of dollars of tokens above those prices through their OpenClaw (and similar autonomous) agents. This was an unsustainable position for Anthropic's finances and its limited compute infrastructure.

stories.headline: FDA Approves Two First-in-Class Cancer Therapies, Beqalzi and Inqovi-Venetoclax Combo

key_facts.fact: The FDA granted accelerated approval to BeOne Medicines' Beqalzi (sonrotoclax), the first BCL2 inhibitor for adults with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of therapy including a BTK inhibitor.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has granted accelerated approval to BEQALZI (sonrotoclax), a foundational, next-generation BCL2 inhibitor, for the treatment of adult patients with relapsed or refractory (R/R) mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), after at least two lines of systemic therapy, including a Bruton's tyrosine kinase (BTK) inhibitor.

key_facts.fact: Beqalzi's approval was supported by a Phase 1/2 study showing a 52% overall response rate, a 16% complete response rate, and a median duration of response of 15.8 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Overall response rate (ORR): 52% (95% CI, 42-62); Complete response (CR) rate: 16% (95% CI, 9.1-24.0); Median duration of response (DOR): 15.8 months.

key_facts.fact: Beqalzi is the 14th novel drug approval of 2026, per the FDA's Novel Drug Approvals list, approved 5/13/2026.
key_facts.excerpt: 14. Beqalzi | sonrotoclax | 5/13/2026 | To treat adults with relapsed or refractory mantle cell lymphoma after at least two lines of systemic therapy, including a Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

key_facts.fact: Separately on May 13, the FDA approved Taiho Oncology's Inqovi (decitabine and cedazuridine) plus venetoclax, the first all-oral combination regimen for newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia in patients 75 or older or ineligible for intensive chemotherapy.
key_facts.excerpt: the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved INQOVI (decitabine and cedazuridine) plus venetoclax as a treatment for adults with newly diagnosed acute myeloid leukemia (AML) who are 75 years or older or who are ineligible for intensive induction chemotherapy. INQOVI in combination with venetoclax is the first and only all-oral combination treatment regimen approved for this patient population.

key_facts.fact: In the supporting trial, the Inqovi-venetoclax combination produced a 41.6% complete remission rate and a median overall survival of 15.5 months.
key_facts.excerpt: Among efficacy-evaluable patients, 42 achieved a CR (41.6%; 95% CI, 31.9-51.8)... Median overall survival was 15.5 months—outcomes that compare favorably with the parenteral azacitidine plus venetoclax regimen from VIALE-A.

stories.headline: Russian Parliament Passes Bill Allowing Putin to Order Invasions of Foreign Countries

key_facts.fact: Russia's parliament approved a bill on May 13 that allows President Vladimir Putin to order the invasion of foreign countries.
key_facts.excerpt: Russia's parliament approved a bill on Wednesday that allows President Vladimir Putin to order the invasion of foreign countries.

key_facts.fact: The bill legally permits Moscow to send troops abroad to protect Russian citizens who are arrested, investigated, put on trial or abused by foreign states, international courts and organizations Russia doesn't belong to.
key_facts.excerpt: Moscow will be legally allowed to send troops abroad to protect Russian citizens who are arrested, investigated, put on trial or abused in any way by foreign states, international courts and organizations that Russia doesn't belong to.

key_facts.fact: Putin has 14 days to sign the bill into law.
key_facts.excerpt: Putin has 14 days to sign the bill into law.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine criticized the measure, with a foreign ministry spokesman saying the State Duma had decided to act as a 'factory for legalizing political adventures, occupation and terror.'
key_facts.excerpt: the Duma's new bill was seen in Kyiv as confirming the 'further militarization of Russian policy'... 'The current composition of the State Duma of the Russian Federation has decided to go down in history as a factory for legalizing political adventures, occupation and terror.'

stories.headline: US Has Cleared ~10 Chinese Firms to Buy Nvidia H200, But No Chips Have Shipped

key_facts.fact: The US has cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's H200 AI accelerator, but not a single chip has been delivered, according to three people briefed on the licences, first reported by Reuters on May 14.
key_facts.excerpt: The US has cleared roughly 10 Chinese companies to buy Nvidia's H200, the company's second-most powerful AI accelerator, but not a single chip has been delivered, according to three people briefed on the licences and first reported by Reuters on 14 May.

key_facts.fact: The US Commerce Department licences cover Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance and JD.com, alongside distributors including Lenovo and Foxconn, with each cleared customer permitted to buy up to 75,000 H200 units.
key_facts.excerpt: The approvals from the US Commerce Department cover Alibaba, Tencent, ByteDance, and JD.com, alongside a handful of distributors, including Lenovo and Foxconn. Each cleared customer is permitted to buy up to 75,000 H200s under the licence terms.

key_facts.fact: Chinese buyers have held back after Beijing told domestic tech firms to pause H200 orders and pushed a parallel supply-chain security review to reduce dependence on US chips.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese buyers have held back after Beijing told domestic technology firms to pause H200 orders earlier this year, with the State Council pushing a parallel supply-chain security review aimed at reducing dependence on US chips.

key_facts.fact: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick told a Senate hearing that the Chinese government has inhibited the purchases to protect its domestic chip industry; the Trump deal also requires 25% of chip-sale revenue to be paid to the US.
key_facts.excerpt: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick addressed the situation during a Senate hearing, noting that the Chinese government has inhibited these purchases to protect internal investments... The deal requires 25 percent of the revenue from chip sales to be paid to the US.

stories.headline: Trump and Xi Open Two-Day Beijing Summit; Xi Warns on Taiwan, Sides Agree on Hormuz

key_facts.fact: Trump and Xi Jinping opened a two-day summit in Beijing on Thursday, May 14, 2026 — the first visit by a sitting US president to the Chinese capital since 2017 — with about two hours and 15 minutes of talks at the Great Hall of the People.
key_facts.excerpt: China's Xi Jinping told President Donald Trump that trade talks were making progress at the start of a two-day summit on Thursday... the Chinese readout of the talks, which concluded after a little over two hours.

key_facts.fact: Xi told Trump that Taiwan is the most important issue in US-China relations and that if it is not handled properly the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy.
key_facts.excerpt: Xi stressed to Mr. Trump that 'the Taiwan question is the most important issue in China-U.S. relations... Otherwise, the two countries will have clashes and even conflicts, putting the entire relationship in great jeopardy.'

key_facts.fact: The White House readout made no mention of Taiwan and focused on Iran: both sides agreed the Strait of Hormuz must remain open, that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon, and Xi expressed interest in buying more American oil to reduce China's dependence on the Strait.
key_facts.excerpt: On Iran, the White House said the two leaders 'agreed that the Strait of Hormuz must remain open to support the free flow of energy... he expressed interest in purchasing more American oil... Both countries agreed that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon.'

key_facts.fact: Xi said US-China economic and trade teams meeting in South Korea had reached 'overall balanced and positive outcomes'; the two sides also discussed creating a US-China Board of Trade and Board of Investment.
key_facts.excerpt: Xi said negotiations between U.S. and Chinese economic and trade teams in South Korea on Wednesday had reached 'overall balanced and positive outcomes,' according to a readout by China's foreign ministry.

key_facts.fact: Trump brought a delegation of US executives to Beijing including Elon Musk, Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Apple's Tim Cook, and said his first request to Xi would be to 'open up' China to American business on a 'totally reciprocal' basis.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump voiced optimism over the future of the bilateral relationship... 'They look forward to trade and doing business, and it's going to be totally reciprocal on our behalf,' he said.
